title: Unit – 1 : Session – 5 : SLO – 2 | Compare Paradigms
sections: 1) OOP vs functional in Java — OOP: objects carry mutable state and behavior; class Counter { int n=0; void inc(){ n++; } }. Functional: stateless pure transformations; IntUnaryOperator inc = n -> n + 1; list.stream().map(inc).forEach(...). OOP emphasizes encapsulation and identity; functional emphasizes immutability and composition.

2) Same problem (sum of even numbers) — Procedural: int s=0; for(int x: arr) if(x%2==0) s+=x; OO/functional style: int s = Arrays.stream(arr).filter(x -> x%2==0).sum(); — the first states how step-by-step; the second declares what to compute.

3) Declarative strengths: concise, readable, closer to problem domain, easier parallelization. Weaknesses: less control over performance, harder debugging of hidden control flow. Imperative strengths: full control, predictable performance, maps to hardware. Weaknesses: verbose, error-prone state management.
